doc.title: Derrick Gardner interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, May 9, 2013

title: The difficulty of keeping the Jazz Prophets working
summary: Without a label, publicist or agent it is hard to find paying work for the sextet, so they play a few gigs a year.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Managers, bookers and the business of getting work

blocks.x: Yeah, as I said, I’m jealous. Well then to jump ahead a few years. What’s it like, you have this group called the Jazz Prophets.
What’s it like these days to try to keep a core of musicians together to carry out a project like that. Everybody is, by necessity, probably doing multiple things, including yourself. Is it hard?

Oh it’s extremely difficult. Without the financial backing of a record label — but there are ways around that as well — or the support of a publicity team, or a booking agent/manager, those type of supporting figures, an IT person for your website, you know, all those things. And it took me a long time to figure out that that’s what was needed. And I finally got to have a few of those pieces in place. It’s still very difficult to find work for the ensemble, or the type of work that I would like to have, that pays for everything. You know, it pays for the travel, the lodging, and all the other specifics, and the musician fees as well. And so those are the jobs that I’m holding out for. I could work quite a bit more but the money wouldn’t be right and the travel situation wouldn’t be right, hotels wouldn’t be right. That would have to come out of my pocket too, to cover some of those expenses so I’d just end up losing a lot of money. And I’ve seen it work for © Hamilton College Jazz Archive -6-

many other artists who carry their own bands and so that’s what I’m trying to do, to do the same thing on my own. And I’m pretty close to figuring it out. In the meantime I just have to work in this kind of sporadic schedule where there’s maybe two or three gigs that we do per year come through everything that’s in place and everything is right.
